newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures retain strong gains at close.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures retain strong gains at close.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended at a four-and-a-half month high on Tuesday as Tokyo players returned from a holiday and sought to catch up with Wall Street's hefty gains since last week.
After opening over 330 points above its previous close of 19,570, the lead Nikkei 225 June contract headed firmly above the psychological 20,000 points level to end at 20,250.
The last time the front Nikkei futures contract closed higher was on December 17, 1996 when it ended at 20,375.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei share average ended 666.17 points up at 20,180.92.
"The Dow went to a record high again yesterday so people were covering their shorts because the Nikkei didn't go up so much on Friday," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
Dealers said stop-loss buying orders were triggered above the 20,000 level, but players started to cash in their gains above 20,250.
"A lot of people are saying it's going to reach 20,500 now but I think it might first go down to cover a gap near 19,570," the trader said.
"The resistance level just below 19,900 has now become a support area. And when the market took out 20,100-20,150, it brought in more buyers," a trader with a local institution said.
Dealers said market sentiment appeared to have turned bullish but further yen strength could cap the Nikkei's upside.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 341.6 against its opening 339.4 on volume of 835 lots.
